default.audience: Web3 developers and institutional finance operators
principles: Translate the product meaning, not the English sentence word for word.
Prefer concise, natural interface copy over formal or literary language.
Keep product names, protocol names, code, identifiers, placeholders, and URLs unchanged.
Use nearby approved translations to keep terminology and tone consistent.

voice: Use natural professional French and address the user with vous.
Keep established Web3 terms in English when French practitioners normally use the English term.
Use French financial vocabulary when it is genuinely standard, such as actif and contrepartie.

terminology.note: Token is the established Web3 product noun. Use French grammar around it.
Wallet is the established product noun in this dashboard.
Keep protocol action names recognizable; write natural French around them, for example minter des Tokens.
Keep the neutral technical terms used by the product.

terminology.preferred: Keep these established technical terms unchanged.

terminology.avoid: point de terminaison / bac à sable API
terminology.note: Use the established developer-facing product terms.
These have natural, standard French financial equivalents.
Use the standard French product and financial terms, including in API error copy.
Use the verb or noun that fits the sentence; do not insert the English word into French grammar.

terminology.preferred: custody for a product category; conservation in explanatory prose
terminology.note: Choose from context instead of forcing one translation everywhere.
